topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the learning objectives and framing the study of cancer genetics and cellular transformation.

topics.label: Tumor viruses and experimental assays for cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the historical discovery of tumor viruses, how they capture cellular proto-oncogenes, and the laboratory assays used to measure oncogenic cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and functional mechanisms of cancer gene mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the categories of cancer-associated mutations and demonstrate their functional consequences in cell cycle control and dominant-negative phenotypes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genomic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the underlying causes of sequence and chromosomal instability, highlighting defective DNA repair pathways and mitotic segregation errors.

topics.label: Stepwise tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations accumulate across stages of tumorigenesis and how inherited cancer syndromes accelerate tumor development.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with administrative wrap-up, recommended reading, and a preview of the next session.
